text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — geo-dns resolver errors (eu-west-1). Alert: geo-resolver-srvfail-rate > 5% for 3 consecutive mins. Affected: model-serving endpoints behind geo load balancer. Observed symptom: bursts of SERVFAIL/timeout from external resolvers (Cloudflare) causing ~30% request failures for some customers. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geodns 

alex: I'm oncall. Starting triage. Can someone grab resolver logs and confirm which resolvers are returning SERVFAILs? @maria?

maria: grabbing logs now. Quick check shows Cloudflare edge resolvers returning a mix of SERVFAIL and NXDOMAIN toward our geo answers, while Route53 answers look fine from our side. TTLs for affected records are 300.

paul: support sees ~12 customers with elevated error rates, 4 enterprise with repeated failures. CS initiated outreach to top 4.

sre-oncall: can you paste a quick `dig` result? I want to rule out our origin config.

maria: running checks — output pasted:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.service.redwood.ai A +short
<empty> (timeout)
; when it responds:
192.0.2.45
```
Responses are intermittent from Cloudflare resolvers, sometimes returning blank / SERVFAIL. Route53 authoritative returns correct sets consistently when queried directly.

alex: OK that suggests CF resolver path is having cache/propagation issues, probably sticky caches returning old/invalid negative entries. This smells like external resolver cache divergence after a recent ANAME swap last night.

tina: I can push a config to our GeoDNS policy to prefer Route53 endpoints for eu-west while we stabilize. Proposing steps: 1) lower GeoDNS TTL to 30s, 2) enforce Route53 primary priority for eu-west, 3) trigger Cloudflare purge for the specific hostnames, 4) open vendor ticket with Cloudflare. Anyone object?

support-lead: do it. Customer impact is non-trivial. Keep CS updated.

paul: opening CF ticket now — ticket #CF-842193. Noted intermittent SERVFAIL from CF resolvers; attaching query samples and resolver IPs.

maria: executing quick purge via Cloudflare API for `api.service.redwood.ai` to clear negative cache. Command:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone>/purge_cache" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --data '{"files":["https://api.service.redwood.ai/"]}'
```
Response: 200 OK queued.

tina: changing geodns policy now — rolling prefer-route53 for eu-west and lowering TTL. Pushing change to k8s config map: `geodns-policy: eu-west: prefer: route53 ttl: 30` then reloading controller.

alex: monitoring metrics. Live dashboard shows error rate dropping from 28% -> 8% over last 2 mins since TTL lowered and purge. Still seeing small spike windows.

sre-oncall: I've kicked off a targeted canary to route 10% traffic to an alternative resolver pool (internal-resolver-proxy) that we control as a stopgap. No config change for customers needed.

support-lead: CS updated: affected customers received notice and mitigation ETA 15m. Severity set to SEV2.

paul: CF replied: investigating potential resolver cache corruption, asked for packet captures from resolver IPs. Sent over query logs.

alex: action items for now (short):
- (maria) keep CF ticket open and push logs (in progress)
- (tina) keep geodns pref on Route53 + TTL 30 until CF confirms fix
- (sre-oncall) monitor canary + metrics, rollback if any regression
- (paul) coordinate CS comms and collect customer manifest for postmortem

maria: noted. Also seeing small number of queries still landing at CF returning SERVFAIL, but frequency is <5% now.

tina: I'll keep the route53 preference for 2h and then slowly relax TTL back to 300 after stable 30m window.

alex: declaring incident and assigning Sev2. Launcher: incidents-bot, runbook used: geodns-resolver. Keep updates in thread every 10m.

incidents-bot: Incident declared SEV2 (geo-dns/resolver). On-call rotation updated: paging secondary oncall. Please post updates here. :eyes:
